summary: Daiki Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He held posts as an instructor at Taisho University (attested 2015, 2026) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, and under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, under Kosen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He was a professor at Otani University and taught at Columbia University.

Daishun Ueyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University, serving as associate professor, professor, and president from 1999 to 2003.

Daito Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Ryukoku and Otani Universities. He taught at Komazawa University (~1904–1927), Toyo University (~1906–1927), Rissho University (~1924–1927), and the University of Tokyo (1923).

Daiun Sogaku Harada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, and under Dokutan Sōsan and Sotan Oka, among others. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who studied under Alan Anderson, W. Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann. He served as a professor of religious studies and Asian studies at Occidental College (~1980–2017).

Dalsukh Malvania was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Banaras Hindu University (~1948–1956), served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (~1957–1973), and held posts at the University of Toronto and MS University of Baroda.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He served as Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).
Dan Li is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso. Li serves as an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2026).

Dan Lusthaus is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Temple University. He held teaching posts at Grinnell College, Bates College, the University of Georgia, and served as a research associate at Harvard University.

Dan Martin is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under Elliot Sperling and others. He held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters and Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Dan Smyer Yü is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and his habilitation from the University of Copenhagen. He has held directorships at Copenhagen and the Center for Subjectivity Research, and a professorship at Oxford.

Daniel A. Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago, later serving on the faculties of McGill University and the University of Chicago.

Daniel Aaron Getz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has held a post as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
